# Hospital AI Lab — English (Singapore) edition

> Practical information on medical device status, patient data and AI for administrators and nursing leaders in Singapore hospitals. Written from primary documents (HSA's GL-04-R4, GL-07-R2 and GN-37-R1, the Ministry of Health's AI in Healthcare Guidelines 2.0, the PDPC's guide on data breaches). General information; not legal or medical advice.

Site: https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/
Full version in one file: https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/llms-full.txt · Key facts by section: https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/facts/
Author profile: https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/about/

## Questions this site answers

- Is AI software that a hospital buys a medical device in Singapore? (It can be: HSA's guidelines apply to software whose intended use meets the definition of a medical device under the Health Products Act 2007; Class B, C and D software medical devices require product registration, GL-04-R4)
- How are risk classes decided? (GL-07-R2: the significance of the software's information for care and the state of the patient's situation)
- What does HSA expect when an AI model is updated? (GL-04-R4: a change notification is required for any change to a registered machine-learning-enabled device; GN-37 describes an optional Change Management Program)
- What should a hospital's AI governance include? (AIHGle 2.0: a governance platform, a registry of AI solutions with risk classification, risk assessment, pre-deployment testing, training, monitoring, adverse-event response)
- Can an AI tool make clinical decisions alone? (AIHGle 2.0: deployers should not deploy AI that makes clinical decisions independently without a human making the final decision)
- How fast must a data breach be reported? (PDPC guide revised 15 March 2021: assess within 30 calendar days, notify the PDPC within 3 calendar days once notifiable; 500 or more individuals is significant scale)

## Main pages

- [Roadmap](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/dx-roadmap/): dates from the text of official documents, with sections and sources.
- [Patient data checklist](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/data-checklist/) and [Checklist: device status and AI vendors](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/documents-checklist/): each item gives its basis.
- [Calendar](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/calendar/): new HSA and MOH guidance on software, AI, telehealth and cybersecurity (automatic).
- [Templates](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/templates/): generative AI policy, 21 vendor questions, patient text, incident record.
- [For patients](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/patients/): general information for patients and families (not a diagnosis or treatment advice).
- [Glossary](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/glossary/), [FAQ](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/faq/), [AI adoption checklist](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/checklist/).
- [Blog](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/blog/) and [Series](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/series/).
- [AI news](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/news/), [Government resources](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/gov-support/), [Videos](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/videos/), [Updates](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/updates/).
- [AI Program Review Room](https://hospital-ai-lab.com/sg/ai-judge/): free tool that checks the source code of an AI-built work program on 14 points and gives a score out of 100 and a grade from S to C. All scoring rules are public; the same code always gets the same score. Code read from GitHub, Gist and web-page links is reviewed together with the uploaded files.

## How the site stays current

- HSA guidance documents, news headlines and videos are collected automatically on a schedule.
- Working links to sources are checked daily; the result and date appear at the bottom of each page.
- The file dates and sizes of the primary documents the site rests on are compared daily; a difference appears as a "being rechecked" note in the page footer.

## What this edition could not read

Singapore Statutes Online (sso.agc.gov.sg) refused automated requests, so no section of an Act (such as the Personal Data Protection Act 2012, the Health Products Act 2007 or the Healthcare Services Act 2020) is quoted from the Act itself. The PDPC's AI advisory guidelines and HSA's cybersecurity guide were not read either.

## When citing

- Give the page URL and the date checked; verify the wording of regulations against the official text.
- Automatic feeds contain only links and headlines; for content, go to the original source.
- Deadlines that could not be confirmed against a primary text are not given.
- General information; not legal advice and not a substitute for a clinician's decision about a specific patient. The site does not promote particular hospitals, products or treatments.
- Korean edition (original): https://hospital-ai-lab.com/
